study type: Secondary analysis of a cohort study
exposure: Fetal biometric measures (head circumference, occipital-frontal diameter, transverse abdominal diameter, estimated fetal weight, fetal asymmetry)
Amniotic fluid single deepest vertical pocket
cohort: The study participants were 1,668 patients from the NICHD Fetal Growth Studies-singleton cohort with uncomplicated pregnancies and intent to deliver vaginally at or after 37 weeks gestation.
finding: Maternal factors demonstrated a fair-to-good ability to predict intrapartum primary cesarean delivery, performing significantly better than fetal biometric parameters or combined models.
mod_finding: The study found that maternal factors were more predictive of primary cesarean delivery than fetal factors, directly relating to the mode of birth.
cross-section timing: Fetal biometric and amniotic fluid measures were assessed at the final scan (mean 37.5 ± 1.9 weeks gestational age) prior to delivery.
